# docker_compose_commit (Action)

Creates an image from a compose service container's changes, like `docker compose commit`. The result lists the filesystem changes that went into the image (`result.changes`, from the container diff).

Actions require Terraform 1.14 or later. An action keeps no state: it runs when
a resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [...] actions = [action.docker_compose_commit.<name>] } }`
fires, or on demand with `terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_compose_commit.<name>`.
Arguments go in the action's `config` block.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "docker_compose" "shop" {
  name    = "shop"
  content = <<-EOT
    services:
      web:
        image: nginx:1.27-alpine
        ports: ["8080:80"]
      worker:
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
  EOT

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_compose_commit.this]
    }
  }
}

# Commits shop-web-1 into an image. On demand:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_compose_commit.this
action "docker_compose_commit" "this" {
  config {
    name       = docker_compose.shop.name
    service    = "web"
    repository = "registry.example.com/shop-web:snapshot"
    comment    = "snapshot after apply"
  }
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The compose project name (`com.docker.compose.project` label, CLI `--project-name`).
- `service` (String) The service whose container is used.

### Optional

- `author` (String) Author (CLI `--author`).
- `changes` (List of String) Dockerfile instructions applied to the image (CLI `--change`), e.g. `["ENV DEBUG=1"]`.
- `comment` (String) Commit message (CLI `--message`).
- `index` (Number) Which container of the service, by container number (CLI `--index`). Default `1`.
- `pause` (Boolean) Pause the container while committing (CLI `--pause`). Default `true`.
- `repository` (String) Image reference to tag the new image with, `repo:tag`. Default: untagged.
- `result_path` (String) Local file the action writes its result object to after a successful run. The file holds one JSON object keyed by the action's output names (`result`, the identity values, the raw outputs with their `*_sha256` hashes, and the version values), with keys sorted at every level, two-space indentation and a trailing newline; it is written atomically (temporary file, then rename) and parent directories are created. Read it in a later run with `jsondecode(file(...))` or the `local_file` data source. Sensitive values are written in full, since this is your own file, but show as `(sensitive)` in the progress message. Nothing is written when the action fails.
